ingredients.name: Cooked, chilled rice
ingredients.notes: about 3 cups; must be cooked and refrigerated beforehand, ideally a day old -- warm, freshly cooked rice will turn the dish mushy

ingredients.name: Oil
ingredients.notes: neutral oil, sesame oil, or butter all work

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.notes: beaten; optional for a fully vegan version

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: sliced; a defining ingredient in the Sri Lankan version of this dish

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: add cautiously, since soy sauce already carries salt

steps.instruction: Make sure the rice is fully cooked and chilled beforehand, ideally refrigerated overnight, or for at least 2-4 hours spread out on a tray. Using warm or freshly cooked rice will make the fried rice clump and turn soggy.
Heat half the oil in a large wok over medium heat. Pour in the beaten eggs (if using) and scramble until just set, breaking into small pieces. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok. Add the curry leaves (if using), onion, and garlic, and stir-fry over medium-high heat for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add the carrot and leek, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until they begin to soften but still have some bite.
Add the green beans, bell pepper, and peas (if using). Stir-fry for a further 1-2 minutes, keeping the vegetables crisp-tender.
Add the chilled rice to the wok, breaking up any clumps with the back of the spatula. Toss well over high heat to combine with the vegetables, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, black pepper, and the scrambled egg back into the wok. Toss everything together thoroughly for a further 2-3 minutes, until evenly coated and heated through.
Taste and adjust salt and soy sauce as needed. Serve hot, on its own or alongside devilled chicken, devilled fish, or another Sri Lankan-Chinese fusion dish.

source_site: islandsmile.org, cross-checked against savperera.com, srilankacooking.com, and thecurryclubhomecooking.com for the chilled-rice technique and leek-and-carrot signature ingredients
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 6+ independent sources; while not a traditional Sri Lankan dish (it's a Chinese-influenced import, as multiple sources explicitly note), the heavy use of leek and carrot is consistently cited as the defining Sri Lankan adaptation
notes: Fried rice is explicitly noted by several Sri Lankan food bloggers as not being a traditional Sri Lankan dish, but rather a Chinese-influenced import that has become a beloved fixture at weddings, parties, and restaurants island-wide -- it sits in the same Sri Lankan-Chinese fusion category as devilled chicken/fish and kottu roti. The defining local adaptation, repeatedly highlighted across sources, is the heavy use of leek and carrot, which gives Sri Lankan fried rice a distinct flavour from other Asian fried rice styles. Day-old, chilled rice is considered essential, not optional -- freshly cooked rice contains too much surface moisture and will turn the dish gummy rather than achieving the desired separate, slightly chewy grains.
